note: Adapted from Light's English original description of 1921, there named Kalotermes mcgregori sp. nov.; type locality Culi Culi, Rizal Province, Luzon (McGregor & Light coll.: 3 October 1920 (month 10) No.188, 19 November 1920 (month 11) No.289; also Rosario, Batangas, 25 December 1920 (month 12) No.339), type No. 24. The original calls it the first record of Kalotermes from the Philippines and the second from the Oriental Region, states that the alate is unknown, and describes only the soldier and the 'larvae'. The original measurement table was printed in three columns (short-headed, long-headed with wing pads, wing pads) and its row labels are badly scrambled after OCR (one row reads '2.25/2.00/2.25' with no identifiable label); this entry takes only the rows whose labels are legible and leaves the rest unrestored. The row label of the total-length row came through the OCR as 'ORES FON SU go eel'; from the values 7.00/6.75/9.00 and the following rows it is taken to be the first row of that table.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: All castes flat and broad-bodied, with a long thorax; head and body hairy. Soldier antennae 15—17-segmented, segment 3 heavily chitinized and twice as long as segment 2; the dorsal and lateral rims of the antennal socket projecting; pronotum long and very broad, much wider than the head and strongly arched, the anterior margin deeply concave, the anterolateral regions projecting over the head; the abdominal tergites of the soldier slightly chitinized. Alate unknown. Lives in the trunks of Leucaena glauca Benth.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Posterior part of the head yellow, shading forwards into chestnut; mandibles black; antennae brown at the base, shading towards the apex into a very pale yellow; pronotum, mesonotum and metanotum pale brown; abdominal tergites, tibiae and tarsi yellow tinged with pale brown, the femora paler. Head, body and legs densely covered with micro-hairs of equal length. Head short, thick and slightly inclined downwards, flat below, rounded above at the sides, slightly tapering at both ends, bluntly rounded behind; frons rather steep, its central area slightly concave. In a few soldiers the head is longer, with straight, tapering sides and a truncate end. Mandibles short and thick, the upward bend very pronounced, the apex slightly incurved; the outer surface with a low basal ridge, slightly concave in the middle and convex near the apex; the left mandible slightly longer than the right, its cutting edge with 3 teeth: the apical tooth divided and extending towards the apex, the second tooth triangular and slightly truncate at the end with a low posterior process confined to the dorsal surface of the mandible, the basal tooth large and bluntly triangular; the right mandible with 2 triangular teeth, the apical surface short and the basal surface long, the basal region rough. Labrum about twice as wide as long, reaching the anterior margin of the lower tooth of the right mandible, the sides parallel, the anterolateral corners slightly rounded, the anterior margin slightly convex with a few setiform hairs. Antennae 15—17-segmented, segment 1 large and cylindrical, almost hidden from above by the projecting dorsal rim of the antennal socket; segment 2 short and cylindrical; segment 3 large, heavily chitinized and inverted-conical, its basal diameter less than that of segment 2; the following 6 segments inverted-conical but short and thick; the more distal segments stoutly club-shaped and lightly chitinized, the last segment oval and white. Eye transparent, its distance from the rim of the antennal socket less than its diameter (not distinguishable in long-headed soldiers). Postmentum short and wide, the anterior part less than twice the width of the narrowest part. Legs short, the femora inflated. Pronotum large, distinctly wider than the head and very arched, nearly semicircular in cross-section; the anterior margin without a median notch but deeply concave, the rounded anterior corners projecting far over the posterolateral regions of the head; the median longitudinal line distinct; widest on the line level with the middle of the anterior margin; the lateral margins receding backwards and meeting the nearly straight, slightly bowed posterior margin; the anterior margin slightly upturned, with a dark brown rim. Mesonotum about two thirds of the length of the pronotum, its posterior margin notched; metanotum shorter than the mesonotum. Body distinctly flat; in dorsal view the thorax and the abdomen of equal length. Almost all soldiers collected have wing pads of unequal size. Measurements (mm, the original table printed in three columns: short-headed, long-headed with wing pads, wing pads; the original table is badly damaged after OCR, so only rows with legible labels are taken): total length 7.00—9.00; head length (without the mandibles) 2.00—2.50; head width 1.70—1.85; pronotum length 1.10—1.25; mandible length (dissected) 1.25—1.50, the right mandible 1.25.

sections.label: Nymph
sections.text: (In the original: Larve.) Large, broad and thick. Antennae 11—17-segmented; with 17 segments, segments 2 and 3 not completely separated; the remaining segments short and stoutly club-shaped, thick distally and narrow proximally, or nearly circular.
